## Install {.i-download}

::: {.starts}

::: {.start}
### Download Emaki

For macOS, Windows and Linux.

{{< include ../_download-step.html >}}
:::

::: {.start}
### Install the agents

Emaki works with Claude Code and Codex.

::: {.start-links}
[Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code){.pill .i-claude} [Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli){.pill .i-codex}
:::
:::

::: {.start}
### Git (optional)

Install Git and the GitHub CLI to commit, branch and push from Emaki.

::: {.start-links}
[Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads){.pill .i-git-branch .pill-git} [GitHub](https://cli.github.com){.pill .i-github .pill-github}
:::
:::

:::

The Agents page ([⌘E]{.kbd}) checks whether your agents and Git are installed and walks you through installing them.

## Open a project {.i-folder}

Choose a folder, pick an agent, and type your first prompt. That starts a session in the folder, with a tab and a row in the sidebar. To pick up an older one, find it in the sidebar: every session on this computer is listed under its project, from both agents.

On the first launch, Emaki copies every Claude Code session into `~/.emaki/archive`, and each later launch catches up, so a session Claude Code has deleted is still here. See [Projects](projects.qmd).

## Layout {.i-app-window}

The sidebar and the chat are always there. Two panels are hidden until you need them: the Files Panel opens at the chat's left and the Terminal Panel at its right, each from a button at an end of the strip over the chat. Two more things wait in the chat's margins. The Outline is a drawer that slides out into the left margin, and the Agent CLI, your agent's own screen, takes the chat's place from the right margin and gives it back. Each has a seam in its margin, a line with a knob halfway, which shows when the pointer comes near. [Settings](settings.qmd#panels) puts each on the side you choose.

::: {.layout}

## What Emaki keeps {.i-hard-drive}

Everything Emaki keeps is in `~/.emaki`:

| | |
|---|---|
| `archive/` | every Claude Code session, copied byte for byte |
| `logs/` | each session rendered as markdown |
| `search.db` | the full-text index |
| `config.json` | your settings |

: {.table-keys tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

Codex has its own archiving system, so `archive/` only stores Claude Code sessions.

Emaki changes one setting in Claude Code: its status line, which feeds Emaki's own [status line](chats.qmd#status-line) under the composer. To put yours back, run `emaki-core statusline restore`.
